goal: faithful output-lossless serving acceleration on the decode-bound gemma-4-31B orchestrator
method: n-gram (prompt-lookup) speculative decoding, num_speculative_tokens=5, prompt_lookup 2..4. No draft model (avoids the multimodal restriction that blocked draft-model spec).
env_workaround: n-gram needs numba, which requires NumPy <=2.2, but the venv has 2.4. Installed numpy 2.2.6 into an isolated dir and injected it via PYTHONPATH only for the benchmark vLLM process; the production venv was NOT modified.
gpu: stopped only gpt-oss (8006) -> GPU1 ~77GB free; kanana and others stayed up; gpt-oss restarted after, all endpoints verified 200
output_identity: 10/10 identical, mean char-similarity 1.000 -> LOSSLESS (accuracy preserved exactly)
acceptance: 264 accepted / 986 draft tokens (~27%); higher on structured extraction (output copies query tokens), near-zero benefit on free-form generation
finding: n-gram speculative decoding gives a byte-identical (lossless) ~26% throughput gain and ~21% latency cut on the STRUCTURED query-analysis stage of gemma-4-31B, because those outputs reuse tokens from the prompt (country/keywords), giving high draft acceptance. Free-form answer generation does not benefit (low prompt overlap). vLLM disables async scheduling under n-gram spec, which caps the gain.
significance: This is the accuracy-preserving serving acceleration for the decode-bound orchestrator: keep the same model (retrieval fidelity intact) and speed up its structured critical-path stages losslessly. It targets exactly the query-analysis path (classify/preparation) that runs on every request. Draft-model spec is unusable (gemma-4 multimodal); n-gram is the right fit for the structured stages.
